x: Mo’ Farah was wheeled out now for Newham & Essex Beagles and soon he was rocketing through the field on his way to a 17:23 – the day’s fastest but some way behind the incredible course record of 17:07 by Brighton’s Andy Bristow from 1989.

Marty Dent, running for Australia, had also benefited from a conservative start and placed, 71st and fifth scorer for his team. Hats off to first Briton home Mo’ Farah who went through the field like a dose of salts from 68th on lap 1 to eventually place 10th.

It was the best time on the course since 1989, eclipsing performances by such luminaries as Keith Cullen and Mo’ Farah. But this drama was a minute and a half off the front where Stephen had already sent a determined Phil Wicks on his way.
